original_idl_permission_notices.scope: Evidence for the original IDL itself; no extension XML blanket scope inferred.
Evidence for the original IDL itself; no extension XML blanket scope inferred.

findings: The original input snapshot is 2018-11-01; root LICENSE.txt was introduced 2019-03-30, so the later root grant alone is not assumed to apply retrospectively to every old byte.
All 57 original crate input member SHA-256 values were verified before comparing Git objects and fetching immutable licensed-snapshot raw URLs.
48 input raw SHA-256 values equal those in the licence-introduction snapshot: 47 XML plus one IDL. Seven inputs changed and two are absent at their original paths.
Both original IDLs contain complete publisher permission notices. The remaining unmatched original XML list has eight entries.
Original stylesheet imports standards.xsl and rev_utils.xsl match exact tree Git objects; bounded legal-word searches find no extra grant. This is not universal proof of absence.
All three root licence versions were read in full and are retained with exact raw byte SHA-256; no SPDX identifier or gate recognition is newly assigned by this receipt.
limitations: Byte equality and a later root licence provide candidate evidence for unchanged inputs, not full khronos_api rights closure.
No later licence was substituted for changed/absent old inputs; no permission inferred from code similarity, API names, current search snippets or repository membership alone.
Other independent Khronos/ANGLE input scopes still need complete source and licence reconciliation.
No runtime code, licence selections, source notices, distributions or gate tests changed this turn. Hosted required checks remain separate.
next_actions: Investigate immutable history/relocations and explicit historical scope for the eight unmatched XMLs; preserve their original bytes and contributors.
Complete independent OpenGL, EGL and ANGLE grant obligations before producing a source-bound aggregate notice for khronos_api.
After full closure, require both authentic exact-source notice proof and consumer verification across every release distribution.
